topic.source_contract: Electricity-network policy, strategic planning, connections, consents and land-rights evidence

facts.guard: national need policy is not a site connection offer, consent or delivery date

facts.planning: strategic coordination should consider environmental, community, deliverability, operability and cost impacts
facts.guard: critical national priority does not remove project-specific impact assessment and mitigation

facts.reforms: government response covers wayleaves, land access, substations, overhead lines and thresholds
facts.status: some measures require legislation or implementation
facts.guard: policy commitment is not treated as an enacted right or granted site consent

facts.reform: queue and process reform support viable projects
facts.guard: system reform does not prove capacity or timing for an individual site

facts.current: June 2026 demand-connections reform focuses on viable projects and strategic prioritisation
facts.constraint: network build and nonviable queue projects can delay connections
facts.guard: priority or queue reform is not a firm connection offer or energisation date

scope_guards: National need and Critical National Priority are not treated as site consent.
Strategic network plans are not treated as committed site-level capacity.
A queue position is not treated as a connection agreement or energisation date.
A connection offer is not treated as constructed network reinforcement.
Land access, wayleave, planning consent and connection agreement are kept separate.
Consultation-response reforms are not treated as enacted law before implementation.
Grid proximity is not treated as available electrical capacity.
No score or promotion is written without exact DNO/NESO evidence, offer, milestones, land rights, consents and delivery.
